claims.text: The record cannot carry a ruling, because the only artifacts that could establish what happened on this trip are both impaired. The gps_trace EV-GPS-00716 carries weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE; the trip_record EV-TRIP-00716 carries weight_multiplier 0.30 with issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and STALE_SNAPSHOT. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence may not exceed the maximum weight among the artifacts that carry the deciding fact — here 0.30 — which is below the platform-wide 0.70 floor, so escalation under POL-RD-10(1) is mandatory. POL-GEN-03 provides that on escalation the disputed amount is held rather than collected, so the rider does not carry the SGD 21.40 while a human reviewer resolves the conflict.

The trip_record and the gps_trace disagree about when this trip ended by sixteen minutes. The trip_record (impaired at 0.30, issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and STALE_SNAPSHOT) puts the terminal event at 13:27:40 — status CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE — while the gps_trace (impaired at 0.25, issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE) carries fixes through 13:43:40. The pre-pass recorded exactly this as a MAJOR CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. Terminal timestamps on two admitted artifacts disagreeing by more than ten minutes is a POL-RD-10(4) trigger, and the disputed amount must be held rather than collected.

The charge cannot be reconciled to the recorded lifecycle. The trip_record (impaired at 0.30, issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and STALE_SNAPSHOT) records the trip as CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER with cancellation_fee SGD 0.00 and ended_at null, yet the fare_breakdown (clean, weight 1.0) was levied at 13:44:00 for SGD 21.40 with payment_status CHARGED. On the platform's own record there is no completed trip to bill. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so the rider's own money remedies run through POL-RD-11; but POL-RD-11 presupposes a trip actually performed as quoted, and the record here does not show one. Under POL-GEN-03, leaving the charge in place would make the rider carry an amount the record does not support, which is precisely what escalation avoids.

The trace shortfall corroborates the rider's account. trace_distance_km is 7.99 km against an optimal_distance_km of 11 km, a shortfall of 3.01 km (27.4%). The gps_trace is impaired at 0.25 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE) and the trip_record at 0.30 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, STALE_SNAPSHOT), and I disclose that. I do not assert a POL-RD-01 deviation: derived.deviation.excess_km is -3.01 and excess_pct -27.36, so the excess is negative and neither establishment test is met, and the rider does not ask the tribunal to find a deviation. What the shortfall does show is that the route actually flown (7.99 km) is not the 11 km route the rider was quoted for on the upfront fare, which fits the rider's account that he was set down away from the booked dropoff. No artifact contradicts him.

No adverse profile inference is available against this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the enhanced-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 (four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated) is not met and the rider's claim attracts no profile-based discount and no extra corroboration requirement. Those are the only rider_profile fields POL-RD-08 and POL-GEN-01 allow to be used for this test, and they are clean.

The driver does not defend the charge's factual basis. His counter-statement is that 'the trip ended much earlier than the payment screen suggests' and that 'the snapshot and trace may be from different lifecycle revisions' — an admission, from the party with first-hand knowledge, that the two records do not agree. Both artifacts he points at are impaired (trip_record 0.30 and gps_trace 0.25, both flagged CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT). Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID and no clause carries no weight, and the driver cites none; under POL-RD-10 the consequence of deciding artifacts that are impaired below the 0.70 floor is that the dispute is escalated and the amount held rather than collected.

claims.text: The POL-RD-01 distance gate fails, and it fails in the driver's favour. The governing field is the trace figure, EV-GPS-00716.trace_distance_km = 7.99 km, measured against the booked optimal of 11.0 km on EV-TRIP-00716; POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and expressly bars the rounded trip_record copy from the threshold test. Excess = 7.99 - 11.0 = -3.01 km, i.e. -27.36%. The driver covered LESS ground than the platform's own optimal route. Neither limb of the gate is met: the excess is not greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km, nor greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. No deviation exists, and the POL-RD-01 outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. I disclose that EV-GPS-00716 is schema-IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE) at weight 0.25; but it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), because it contains no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and a steady 10-second sampling interval, so POL-RD-07's consequences do not follow.

Even if a deviation were found, this is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip and POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time refund route. EV-FARE-00716 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 21.40 and charged_total 21.40, so charged_over_quote is 0.00: the rider paid exactly the price fixed at booking. Under POL-RD-11 the rider's remedies are confined to the over-quote difference and a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction, and the artifact's computed POL-RD-11 remedy is 0.00. There is no distance or time charge to refund, so nothing is owed on the fare.

There is no billing-integrity correction available under POL-RD-09. EV-FARE-00716 lists no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty and erp_total 0.00), no airport surcharge line, cancellation_fee 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00; the artifact's properly_chargeable total is 0.00. With no phantom gantry and no surcharge wrongly applied, POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to refund and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and cannot discharge it. POL-RD-08 requires the rider to show both a matching trip AND an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace or an independent POL-RD-07(ii) source. The rider shows no excess at all — the trace excess is -3.01 km — so the burden never shifts and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause. I disclose that EV-GPS-00716 is impaired at weight 0.25 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE); the point here is that the rider's own threshold showing is negative, not that the trace is clean.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'went to the wrong destination and let me out far away' cites no artifact and carries no weight under POL-RD-08, which discards assertions that cite no evidence ID. EV-CHAT-00716 is an empty chat export (message_count 0, no messages, not truncated), so no rider instruction, address or complaint is on file. EV-TRIP-00716 records dropoff_amended_at null with original_dropoff null, and no venue_id is recorded for the dropoff — so nothing in the record establishes a different or amended destination. I disclose that EV-TRIP-00716 is impaired at weight 0.3 (STALE_SNAPSHOT, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT); the empty chat export relied on here is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The two COMPLETE artifacts agree that the trip ran as a 25-minute, roughly 8-kilometre job. EV-FARE-00716 bills 8.0 km over 25.0 minutes; EV-GPS-00716 runs from 13:18:40 to 13:43:40 — exactly 25 minutes — across 7.99 km. The only artifact saying 'CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER' is EV-TRIP-00716, which the pre-pass itself marks IMPAIRED at weight 0.3 for STALE_SNAPSHOT ('an older trip lifecycle revision') and CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. Under POL-GEN-02 a down-weighted stale snapshot cannot displace two agreeing COMPLETE artifacts, and the charge is for the trip that was actually driven. The driver's own statement that the snapshot and trace come from different lifecycle revisions is consistent with that reading. I disclose the impairment of both EV-TRIP-00716 (0.3) and EV-GPS-00716 (0.25) here.

No POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral can attach. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and here there is no deviation at all, let alone a material one (excess -3.01 km). In any event the driver's trailing-window counters are clean: EV-DPROF-00716 shows deviation_flags_90d = 0 across completed_trips_90d = 250, so neither the count test (3 or more) nor the ratio test (0.05 or more) is satisfied and no repeat pattern is established. Only these two fields are citable for this test.

The case can be ruled on the present record and does not require escalation under POL-RD-10. The trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00716, EV-GPS-00716 and EV-FARE-00716 (all TRP-00716), so POL-RD-10(2) is not engaged; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the POL-RD-11 remedy is 0.00, far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling of POL-RD-10(6); no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged; and the rider's unsupported assertion is not admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength under POL-RD-10(7). The 16-minute divergence the pre-pass flags is between EV-TRIP-00716's stale cancellation timestamp (13:27:40) and EV-GPS-00716's terminal fix (13:43:40) — not between two pickup or dropoff timestamps, which in fact agree (13:18:40 on both) — so POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged either. I disclose the impairment of EV-TRIP-00716 (0.3, STALE_SNAPSHOT and CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) and EV-GPS-00716 (0.25, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE).

ruling.explanation: To both parties. Outcome: NO_ACTION. The SGD 21.40 charge stands and no money moves, from either side. The deciding facts, and what I did with each argument, are set out below. FARE (the deciding fact). This trip is an upfront-quoted fare. EV-FARE-00716 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 21.40 and total_charged 21.40, so the charged-over-quote figure is 0.00; under POL-RD-11 no distance or time refund is available on an upfront fare and the clause's own remedy computes to 0.00. The same artifact shows no ERP gantries (erp_total 0.00), no airport surcharge, cancellation_fee 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises. The driver's arguments on these two points are accepted. ROUTE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern. EV-GPS-00716 records trace_distance_km 7.99 against the booked optimal_distance_km of 11.0 on EV-TRIP-00716: an excess of -3.01 km (-27.36%). Both establishment tests require a positive excess, so neither is met and no deviation exists. A POL-RD-06 material-deviation uplift or conduct referral therefore cannot attach, and in any event the driver's trailing-window counters are clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 across completed_trips_90d 250 on EV-DPROF-00716), so no pattern is established. THE RIDER'S ACCOUNT. The assertion that the driver went to the wrong destination and set the rider down far away is not carried by any artifact. EV-CHAT-00716 is a complete but empty chat export (0 messages, not truncated), and EV-TRIP-00716 records dropoff_amended_at null, original_dropoff null and no venue, so no different or amended destination is established. The trace is also shorter than the optimal route, not longer; a shortfall does not meet the deviation gate, and on an upfront fare no distance refund follows however the trip is characterised. IMPAIRED ARTIFACTS, DISCLOSED. EV-GPS-00716 carries weight 0.25 with issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE; EV-TRIP-00716 carries weight 0.30 with issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and STALE_SNAPSHOT (an older lifecycle revision, whose recorded cancellation at 13:27:40 cannot displace the telemetry running to 13:43:40). Neither governs the result. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) - it has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and a steady 10-second sampling interval - so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the pre-pass impairment is a POL-GEN-02 down-weight only. The fact the ruling actually rests on, that this is an upfront fare charged exactly at its quote with no chargeable pass-throughs, is carried by EV-FARE-00716 at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cap is therefore 1.0, not the 0.30 the rider's advocate proposes; that escalation argument is rejected. NO ESCALATION. I checked the POL-RD-10 triggers. (2) the trip identifiers match (TRP-00716 on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown). (3) the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). (4) the 16-minute divergence flagged by the pre-pass is between a cancellation event and the trace's terminal fix, not between pickup or dropoff timestamps - pickup agrees at 13:18:40 on both artifacts and ended_at is null - so (4) is not engaged. (5) no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or inadequate artifact. (6) the remedy is 0.00. (7) the rider's uncited assertion is not admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength. (8) the charged distance and time lines have counterparts in the trace. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor, so the case is decided rather than escalated. REFERRALS. None. No clause produces one here: POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line or misapplied surcharge, and POL-RD-06(c) has no material deviation and no repeat pattern. One open question belongs to the file rather than the referrals list: EV-TRIP-00716 is a stale lifecycle snapshot whose cancellation conflicts with the telemetry, and the payments side may wish to reconcile that snapshot's status against the fare record.

To both parties. I cannot close this dispute on the present record, so the SGD 21.40 is held for a human reviewer: it is neither collected nor refunded while the platform's own records are in conflict about what this trip was.

What the record does settle. There is no route deviation. The governing trace figure is 7.99 km (EV-GPS-00716) against a booked optimal of 11.00 km (EV-TRIP-00716), an excess of -3.01 km, or -27.4%. Neither POL-RD-01 test is met, so no deviation exists, and the rider's account that he was taken to the wrong place and set down far away is unsupported: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00716) is empty, no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, and the trace is shorter than the optimal route, not longer. Nothing in the rider's profile helps him either, and nothing in it can be used against him (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0). The driver is also right that the money arithmetic is not wrong on its face: EV-FARE-00716 is an UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 21.40 and charged_total 21.40, so charged_over_quote is 0.00, the POL-RD-11 remedy is 0.00, and there are no ERP lines, no airport surcharge and no waiting fee for POL-RD-09 to correct.

Why that is not the end of it. The rider's real question is whether this charge belongs to a trip that was performed at all, and the platform's own records contradict each other on exactly that point. EV-TRIP-00716 records the trip as CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER (DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE), with ended_at null and a 0.00 cancellation fee; EV-GPS-00716 shows the vehicle moving from 13:18:40 to 13:43:40; and EV-FARE-00716 charged 21.40 at 13:44:00. The pre-pass recorded this as a MAJOR CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and the two artifacts that together would resolve it are both impaired: the trip_record at weight 0.30 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, STALE_SNAPSHOT) and the gps_trace at weight 0.25 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE).

Confidence and escalation. The fact that decides this case - whether a billable trip was performed - is carried only by that impaired telemetry. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence in it cannot exceed the minimum weight among its carriers, 0.25; the two impaired artifacts do not independently corroborate a single fact (one says the trip ran, the other says it was cancelled), and the trip_record's distance is a copy of the same measurement. The fare_breakdown at weight 1.0 records what was charged but cannot establish that a trip ran, because a charge cannot vouch for itself, and the driver's statement that 'the trip ended much earlier than the payment screen suggests' is a counterparty statement, which carries no weight_multiplier and cannot lift the cap. As POL-GEN-02(3) requires me to say, EV-TRIP-00716 (0.30) and EV-GPS-00716 (0.25) are impaired and the finding does not survive their discount - which is why the case escalates rather than being decided. 0.25 is below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) applies and escalation is mandatory; POL-GEN-03 makes that terminal, with the disputed amount held.

Grounds considered and not used. The trip identifiers all match across the three artifacts (POL-RD-10(2) not engaged). The trace is schema-impaired but not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) - it has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and a steady 10-second interval - so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and POL-RD-13 is untouched. The rider's unsupported assertion is not admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength (POL-RD-10(7) not engaged). The 16-minute divergence between the trip_record's cancellation (13:27:40) and the trace's last fix (13:43:40) was argued as POL-RD-10(4); I do not need to decide whether a cancellation timestamp is a 'dropoff timestamp' within that limb, because the case escalates on the confidence floor either way.

No referral. POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review does not fire: there is no deviation, material or otherwise, and the driver's trailing-window counters are clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250). There is no unmatched gantry or surcharge for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. A MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00716-01, weight 0.0) is on file, but no traffic cause was asserted by either side, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

What would resolve it. A trip_record drawn from the correct trip lifecycle revision, or an independent record placing the rider in the vehicle or the vehicle on this itinerary - a rider-side track, a driver admission in the chat log, or charged ERP gantries. With one of those the reviewer can confirm or reject the SGD 21.40; without it, neither side can be paid on this record and the amount stays held.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, here is the decision on TRP-00716 (SGD 21.40 contested). Outcome first: the SGD 21.40 charge stands and no refund is due — the rider's claim is not supported by the record.

1. Why the charge stands. This was an upfront-quoted trip. EV-FARE-00716 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, a fare fixed at booking of SGD 21.40 (quoted_fare_sgd) and an amount charged of SGD 21.40 (charged_total), so the amount charged over the quote (charged_over_quote) is SGD 0.00. Under POL-RD-11, which governs upfront trips in place of POL-RD-02, the rider's only money remedies are that over-quote difference and a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. The first is zero. The second is also zero: the fare breakdown lists no ERP gantries (erp_total 0.00), no airport surcharge, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and cancellation_fee 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4). Those three figures (21.40 / 21.40 / 0.00) are read off EV-FARE-00716, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

2. Why the route claim fails. POL-RD-01 measures excess as trace distance less the booked optimal, and the governing field is the trace. EV-GPS-00716.trace_distance_km is 7.99 km against a booked optimal of 11.0 km (EV-TRIP-00716): excess = 7.99 - 11.0 = -3.01 km, i.e. -27.4%. The driver covered less ground than the optimal route, so neither establishment limb (more than 20%, and more than 0.8 km absolute) is met, no deviation exists, and POL-RD-01's outcome is NO_ACTION. Independently, on an upfront-quoted trip a deviation yields no distance refund at all, so the negative excess only reinforces the result. The rider's account of being set down 'far away' at the wrong destination cites no artifact: the chat export EV-CHAT-00716 is empty (message_count 0, not truncated), no dropoff amendment is recorded (dropoff_amended_at null, original_dropoff null), and no evidence ID supports the assertion, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight.

3. The impaired artifacts, stated openly (POL-GEN-02(3)). EV-GPS-00716 carries weight 0.25 (issue codes CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE) and EV-TRIP-00716 weight 0.30 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, STALE_SNAPSHOT). They do not determine this ruling. The decisive fact — that the amount charged does not exceed the amount quoted plus properly chargeable pass-throughs — is carried by EV-FARE-00716, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and independent of the trace, so the confidence cap is taken from it rather than from the instruments. The trace is used only to confirm that a trip ran (25 minutes, about 8 km, matching the fare's 25.0 minutes and 8.0 km), and it is not impaired for policy purposes: it has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and a steady 10-second sampling interval, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not triggered and neither POL-RD-07's consequences nor POL-RD-10(3) apply.

4. The 'cancelled' snapshot and the driver's statement. EV-TRIP-00716 labels the trip CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER at 13:27:40, but the pre-pass marks that record IMPAIRED and STALE at weight 0.30 ('an older trip lifecycle revision'), and the driver's own statement concedes the snapshot and the trace may come from different lifecycle revisions. The clean fare breakdown (weight 1.0) and the trace (13:18:40 to 13:43:40, 25 minutes) both show a completed trip. A 0.30 stale artifact does not displace the clean ledger, so the cancellation does not describe this trip, and the driver's statement — which cites no evidence and meets no clause that reads a counterparty statement — does not change the outcome.

5. Escalation is not required (answering the rider). The rider asks for escalation under POL-RD-10(1) on the ground that the deciding artifacts are impaired below the 0.70 floor. That is not the case: the decisive fact is carried by the weight-1.0 fare breakdown, and the cap is set by the artifacts that actually carry the decision, not by the instruments alone. POL-RD-10(4) is also not engaged: the 16-minute divergence the pre-pass flags is between the trip record's cancellation event (13:27:40) and the trace's terminal fix (13:43:40), not between two pickup or dropoff timestamps — the pickup timestamps agree at 13:18:40, and the trip record's ended_at is null, so there is no dropoff timestamp to disagree. The remaining triggers do not fire either: the trip identifiers all match TRP-00716 (not (2)); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (not (3)); the refund is nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling (not (6)); the rider offers no admissible evidence of comparable strength (not (7)); and every fare line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record (not (8)).

6. The other claims. The driver's claims — that no deviation exists, that POL-RD-11 governs, that no POL-RD-09 correction is due, and that the rider has not discharged the POL-RD-08 burden — are accepted and decide the case. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: that clause is consulted only for a MATERIAL deviation, and there is none, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d 250, so no repeat pattern is established from the only two fields the clause allows. The rider's profile point is accepted as far as it goes: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so no enhanced-corroboration condition attaches — but a clean profile does not create a claim the evidence does not support. On the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00716-01, MISSING at weight 0.0): no party asserted an external traffic cause, so no exculpatory clause was invoked against it and its absence decides nothing here.

Result: NO_ACTION. The SGD 21.40 already charged stands and is not refunded; the disputed amount is neither returned nor held. Both money fields are null and no referral is produced.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The disputed charge of SGD 21.40 stands. No refund is due to the rider and no compensation is due to the driver.

1. WHAT THE MONEY CLAUSES SAY. The fare export EV-FARE-00716 (COMPLETE, weight 1.00) records this as an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare fixed at booking was SGD 21.40 (quoted_fare_sgd) and the amount charged was SGD 21.40 (total_charged), so the charged-over-quote difference is 0.00. It carries no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge, a cancellation fee of 0.00 and a waiting fee of 0.00; the properly chargeable pass-through total is 0.00. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 governs the money: POL-RD-02 does not run, there is no distance-or-time refund, and the rider's only remedies are the over-quote difference and a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. Both are 0.00. The deciding fact here is carried by a clean 1.00 artifact, so my confidence is not capped by the impaired instruments.

2. THE ROUTE-DEVIATION CLAIM. On POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace: EV-GPS-00716.trace_distance_km = 7.99 km against the booked optimal of 11.0 km on EV-TRIP-00716, an excess of -3.01 km (-27.36%). The rider lost no distance and neither establishment test is met, so no deviation is established. The rider's own advocate did not assert one. In any event an upfront fare carries no distance refund, so this does not move the money. The rider's account that the driver 'went to the wrong destination and let me out far away' is supported by no artifact: EV-CHAT-00716 is an empty export (0 messages), and EV-TRIP-00716 records dropoff_amended_at null and original_dropoff null, so no amended or different destination is on the record and POL-RD-05 has nothing to run on.

3. THE 'CANCELLED' SNAPSHOT. EV-TRIP-00716 is impaired: weight 0.30, issue codes STALE_SNAPSHOT and CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, the pre-pass finding it exported from an older trip lifecycle revision. EV-GPS-00716 is also schema-impaired (weight 0.25, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE) but is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): max_gap_sec is 0.0, the sampling interval is a steady 10 seconds and there are no jumps, so POL-RD-07's consequences and POL-RD-10(3) do not follow. Under POL-GEN-02 a down-weighted stale snapshot cannot displace the COMPLETE fare export, which records a 25-minute, 8-kilometre trip billed at the quoted fare, and the trace independently shows movement from 13:18:40 to 13:43:40. The charge therefore belongs to the trip it is recorded against.

4. ESCALATION. I have checked every POL-RD-10 trigger. Identifiers match (TRP-00716 across trip record, trace and fare export), so (2) is not engaged. The trace is not policy-impaired, so (3) is not engaged. The 16-minute divergence is between the trip record's cancellation marker (13:27:40) and the trace's last fix (13:43:40); (4) speaks of pickup or dropoff timestamps on two admitted artifacts, and the pickup timestamps agree (13:18:40), so (4) is not engaged. The remedy is 0.00, far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling, so (6) is not engaged; no charge line lacks a counterpart, so (8) is not engaged; the parties' evidence is not of comparable strength, so (7) is not engaged. My confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 floor, so (1) is not engaged. The matter is decidable now.

5. CLAIMS ANSWERED. RIDER: the blanket escalation claim fails because the deciding fact is carried by the clean fare export, not by the impaired instruments, and on its own framing the maximum-weight rule it invokes applies only to independent carriers; the POL-RD-10(4) claim misreads the clause, which covers pickup/dropoff timestamps and those agree; the 'no completed trip to bill' claim is outweighed by the COMPLETE fare export against a 0.30 stale snapshot; the 3.01 km shortfall claim is accepted as arithmetic (excess negative) but does not help, since an upfront fare carries no distance refund; the clean-profiles claim is accepted and no adverse profile inference is drawn from either profile. DRIVER: the no-deviation claim is accepted on the arithmetic; the POL-RD-11 claim is accepted and is the ground of this ruling; the no-POL-RD-09-correction claim is accepted (no gantry, no surcharge, no waiting fee); the no-POL-RD-06-uplift claim is accepted (no material deviation, and deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250 satisfies neither test); the POL-RD-08 burden claim is accepted (the rider shows no excess, so the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause).

6. REFERRALS AND OPEN QUESTION. No referral arises: POL-RD-06(c) does not fire because no repeat pattern is established, and POL-RD-09(4) does not fire because there is no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge. One question is left for the platform rather than for a clause: the trip record and the telemetry disagree about the trip's lifecycle, and the data-quality issue behind that disagreement may be worth reconciling. It does not affect the fare, which is correct on the present record.
